reviewer_notes: This is primarily an EnMS deployment/management paper, not an energy-performance-modelling paper. The only energy performance models are intensity-ratio EnPIs: a lagging EnPI defined corporate-wide as energy/production (Mbtu/ton on p.5; GJ per metric ton for the SC case on p.11), captured as M1 (A1, SC company) and M2 (A2, PTA facility, target 8.5 GJ/ton, Fig.3). The paper also describes a 'leading EnPI' — a composite PDCA self-assessment maturity index (equal 25% weights per PDCA stage; company-wide implementation reached 89%, p.12). It was NOT enveloped as a model because it measures EnMS implementation progress rather than energy performance; the reviewer should decide if it should be treated as a composite-index model. Actual EnPI tracking trends were withheld for confidentiality (p.11). The PTA facility in Fig.3 is cited to ref [31], a study of BP Chemicals (M) Sdn Bhd in Malaysia, so A2's country/region is ambiguous and recorded as not reported.
